FROMGIT: drm/msm: Fix task dump in gpu recovery The current recovery code gets a pointer to the task struct and does a few things all within the rcu_read_lock. This puts constraints on the types of gfp flags that can be used within the rcu lock. This patch instead gets a reference to the task within the rcu lock and releases the lock immediately, this way the task stays afloat until we need it and we also get to use the desired gfp flags. Signed-off-by: Sharat Masetty <smasetty@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@gmail.com> (cherry picked from commit 9f8378afe8b423e21667edb9f0555bb97d7797c7) (am from git://people.freedesktop.org/~robclark/linux) BUG=None TEST=Tested on cheza Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ie5ab5c3de0e3cf875639240951fd2dbf57233947 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1349990 Reviewed-by: Kristian H. FROMGIT: drm/msm/hdmi: Enable HPD after HDMI IRQ is set up SoCs that contain MDP5 have a top level wrapper called MDSS that manages locks, power and irq for the sub-blocks within it. Irq for HDMI is also routed through the MDSS. Shortly after the Hot Plug Detection (HPD) is enabled in HDMI, HDMI interrupts are recieved by the MDSS interrupt handler. However at this moment the HDMI irq is still not mapped to the MDSS irq domain so the HDMI irq handler cannot be called to process the interrupts. This leads to a flood of HDMI interrupts on CPU 0. If we are lucky to have the HDMI initialization running on a different CPU, it will eventually map the HDMI irq to MDSS irq domain, the next HDMI interrupt will be handled by the HDMI irq handler, the interrupt flood will stop and we will recover. If the HDMI initialization is running on CPU 0, then it cannot complete and there is nothing to stop the interrupt flood on CPU 0. The system is stuck. Fix this by moving the HPD enablement after the HDMI irq is mapped to the MDSS irq domain. Signed-off-by: Todor Tomov <todor.tomov@linaro.org> Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@gmail.com> (cherry picked from commit 66b1e71547aa9b681ac5274598e36490e9be21b0) (am from git://people.freedesktop.org/~robclark/linux) BUG=None TEST=Tested on cheza Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ib622934794c9019282fdb5dfa253ba1f8c65b6b2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1350003 Reviewed-by: Kristian H. Kristensen <hoegsberg@chromium.org>

This is done with the intent of introducing "num-mic" and "num-camera" fields to the schema, which will both be set to {{$num-mic}} today. This lets various consumers (audio configuration, ARC++ media profiles, ARC++ hardware features) correctly configure the system for multiple cameras/mics, while keeping the schema free in the future to have different numbers of microphones and cameras. For handling camera, A more ambitious change would be to have the schema add entries like: front_camera: <vid:pid> rear_camera: <vid:pid> ...but I believe that for today, simply knowing the number will be enough. UPSTREAM: xhci: Fix USB3 NULL pointer dereference at logical disconnect. Hub driver will try to disable a USB3 device twice at logical disconnect, racing with xhci_free_dev() callback from the first port disable. This can be triggered with "udisksctl power-off --block-device <disk>" or by writing "1" to the "remove" sysfs file for a USB3 device in 4.17-rc4. USB3 devices don't have a similar disabled link state as USB2 devices, and use a U3 suspended link state instead. In this state the port is still enabled and connected. hub_port_connect() first disconnects the device, then later it notices that device is still enabled (due to U3 states) it will try to disable the port again (set to U3). The xhci_free_dev() called during device disable is async, so checking for existing xhci->devs[i] when setting link state to U3 the second time was successful, even if device was being freed. The regression was caused by, and whole thing revealed by, Commit 44a182b9d177 ("xhci: Fix use-after-free in xhci_free_virt_device") which sets xhci->devs[i]->udev to NULL before xhci_virt_dev() returned. and causes a NULL pointer dereference the second time we try to set U3. Fix this by checking xhci->devs[i]->udev exists before setting link state. The original patch went to stable so this fix needs to be applied there as well. shill: fixup Nl80211Frame parsing The frame length handling in the Nl80211Frame() constructor was a little imprecise. It checked for a minimum length that included the header and 16 bits of body, but some of these frames utilize fields that are past the 16-bit boundary. Let's refactor the struct to group the header and body fields differently, and split the bounds-checking to (a) initial header check and (b) per-frame-type body length check Doing this kills the general "kMinimumFrameByteCount", and we just require that all frames have the 24-byte minimum header instead. Along the way, I also * fix the endianness handling on frame_control (we need to convert fields larger than a byte from LE to native endianness) * avoid duplicating the frame_type extraction in ToString() The latter point helps avoid duplicating the bounds checks too, since we can just declare the "type" as invalid in the constructor. Lastly, make the packed alignment explicit and add a couple of sanity checks in the unit tests. We currently are at the mercy of the compiler to keep our 16-bit / 8-bit fields matching the 802.11 frame format. BUG=chromium:907847 TEST=unit tests; fuzzer targets; watch net.log on a device Change-Id: I87f9a5e82d586f0f3fac87cf96a93acc30d84b3d Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1351120 Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org>

common-mk: Bind-mount /run/shm for unit tests On some systems /dev/shm is a symlink to /run/shm/. This is currently the case on bots that run Chrome OS unit tests. On such systems the tests that rely on /dev/shm, like when the tested code uses libchrome's shared memory functionality, were broken since /run/shm isn't currently bind-mounted by platform2_test.py and therefore /dev/shm is an invalid location. Fix this by bind-mounting /run/shm in platform2_test.py. However, skip bind-mounting this when it's a symlink itself (as on modern Ubuntu /run/shm is, the other way round, a symlink to /dev/shm). BUG=chromium:903799,chromium:893756 TEST=existing platform2 unit tests, run with reenabled unit tests in the diagnostics package that used base::SharedMemory (i.e., with revert of CL:1327083) Change-Id: I34e4e0c8bd4ef413ddf143c62f61760996d50f19 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1335791 Commit-Ready: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Tested-by: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org>
